name: Freight Quote Requests
trigger: An Account Manager needs a freight quote for a shipment between two locations on a client project.
purpose: Getting quotes from both vendors and reviewing them with Sienna before anything goes to the client keeps pricing consistent and catches problems before they reach the account. Scope: any AM requesting LTL or dedicated freight quotes for a client shipment.
doneWhen: Both vendors have responded, Sienna and the AM have agreed on which option to present, and a recommendation is ready for the client.
timeToRun: 15 minutes to send requests, plus vendor response time

steps.title: Confirm the project code in Portal
steps.trigger: A client shipment needs a quote; you have pickup and delivery addresses and the requested pickup window.
steps.work: Look up the project's code in Portal. It goes in the subject line of both quote request emails.

steps.title: Are pallet count and weight known?
steps.work: If the client gave real dimensions and weight, or the items are already palletized, proceed. If manifest details are incomplete or unclear, ask the client for real dimensions and weight before falling back to an estimate.

steps.title: Estimate pallets and weight with Claude
steps.trigger: Dimensions and weight are unknown and the items are not palletized.
steps.work: Paste the item manifest into Claude and ask for an educated guess on total pallets and weight.

steps.title: Send the same request to both vendors, CC Sienna
steps.trigger: Project code and shipment details are ready.
steps.work: Email Unishippers (Alex O'Reilly) and Flock Freight (Tucker Morris) with the identical request, CC Sienna. Subject: Build Dynamics [Client: {Client}] | Project Code = {Code} | New Quote Request | {Origin} to {Destination}. Ask for LTL and Dedicated quotes; include addresses, dates and windows, the manifest with dimensions or pallet count and total weight, whether palletized (ask for driver assist if not), and an Item / Qty Confirmed table.

steps.title: Have both vendors responded?
steps.work: Wait for both quotes. If a vendor hasn't responded, follow up directly and loop in Sienna if it is holding up the timeline.

steps.title: Follow up with the vendor
steps.work: Follow up directly with the vendor contact; loop in Sienna if the delay threatens the client's timeline.

steps.title: Review both quotes with Sienna
steps.work: Huddle with Sienna to compare LTL and dedicated pricing from both vendors and agree on what to present.

steps.title: What are we presenting to the client?
steps.work: Check both: compared both vendors' LTL and dedicated pricing; picked the option that fits the client's timeline. If unsure who else to loop in, the owner has not yet filled that in.

steps.title: Present the recommendation to the client
steps.trigger: Sienna and the AM agree on the option.
steps.work: Present the agreed recommendation and pricing to the client.
